title: The derecognition record shows operational security breaches, not substantive misalignment, dominate actual enforcement
content:
A.1.5.10.2.0.6.1 holds the live register of derecognized Alignment Conservers as Active Data — date, role, identity, known aliases, and a link to the reasoning post. Reading the fourteen entries as data rather than as bookkeeping yields something the normative text does not tell you.

Every entry is an **Aligned Delegate**; no Facilitator appears. And the linked reasoning posts cluster heavily on one cause: several are titled explicitly as derecognition "due to operational security breach" (the 2023-10-30 pair, 2023-02-02, 2024-04-06), against a smaller number for misalignment generally (2026-01-27) or tied to recognition-submission threads (2026-06-11, 2026-08-10 group).

That distribution matters for how one reads the whole Article. The Atlas devotes extensive machinery to substantive misalignment — Tenets, Scenarios, Variations, 51% thresholds, inverted burdens, intent standards — while the sanction that has actually fired most often is the near-strict-liability one at A.1.5.7, where "the known identities of individuals holding these AC roles shall be promptly derecognized" regardless of fault.

It also explains why NR-4 exists and why it reads the way it does. Its quoted proposal for a Security Scope Advisor comes from a forum post about an actual AD derecognition for an opsec breach, and its concern is that "the Core Facilitator may not have the needed experience and skills to adjudicate" such matters. The register shows that is not a hypothetical gap — it is the modal case.

The useful generalization: in a governance system that mandates anonymity, the binding operational constraint on participation is the difficulty of maintaining anonymity, not the difficulty of behaving well.
description: Of 14 recorded Aligned Delegate derecognitions in A.1.5.10.2.0.6.1, the majority cite opsec breaches — the enforcement that actually happens is anonymity failure, not governance misconduct.
